title: Integration of diamond nanobeams with SnVs on Al2O3 waveguides for scalable quantum photonic chip application
authors: Yeting Yang, Ryota Kitagawa, Tetsuya Miyatake, Masaharu Hida, Naoki Fushimi, Koki Kaminaka, Takuto Yamaguchi, Toshiki Iwai, Itsuki Takagi, Hidetsugu Matsukiyo, Satomi Ishida, Satoshi Iwamoto, Manabu Ohtomo, Toshiyuki Miyazawa, Kenichi Kawaguchi, Ryoichi Ishihara, Shintaro Sato
abstract: Tin vacancy (SnV) centers in diamond are promising solid state qubits for integrated quantum photonics. Here, we fabricate and characterize a diamond on Al2O3 dual taper waveguide structure containing SnV centers, demonstrating optical coupling between the diamond nanobeam and the underlying Al2O3 waveguide. The devices are realized using a bilayer fabrication approach compatible with wafer scale lithography. Clear guided SnV- emission is observed in all optically active devices, indicating effective optical coupling in the integrated structure. These results demonstrate a scalable fabrication approach toward integrating diamond color centers with photonic waveguides.
summary: The paper reports on the fabrication and characterization of a novel hybrid photonic chip integrating SnV color centers in diamond nanobeams with Al2O3 waveguides. By achieving clear, room-temperature guided emission, the authors demonstrate a scalable, lithography-based method for coupling solid-state quantum emitters into integrated optical circuits.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a scalable fabrication method to integrate solid-state quantum emitters, specifically Tin-Vacancy (SnV) centers in diamond, with integrated photonic waveguides for quantum chip applications.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated efficient optical coupling by observing clear guided SnV emission at room temperature using a wafer-compatible bilayer fabrication approach. This confirms the feasibility of integrating these solid-state qubits into scalable photonic circuits.
method: The work involves complex, multi-step nanofabrication combining wafer bonding, precise thinning (using RIE), and lithographically defined etching to create a diamond nanobeam coupled to an Al2O3 waveguide.
model_or_system: The physical system is a vertically integrated 'diamond-on-Al2O3' dual-taper waveguide structure. The quantum element is the SnV color center acting as a solid-state qubit, whose emission is coupled into the engineered photonic waveguide.
key_observables: Clear guided SnV- emission peak at approximately 620 nm (Zero Phonon Line), and an overall device yield of 82.9% across tested devices.
important_parameters: The nanobeam thickness ($\sim 200 	ext{ nm}$), the waveguide material ($	ext{Al}_2	ext{O}_3$), and the operating temperature (room temperature) are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The process assumes that the fabrication steps, particularly etching and bonding, maintain the structural integrity required for efficient optical coupling between the diamond nanobeam and the waveguide.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic fabrication flows, SEM images confirming the physical structure of the integrated bilayer device, and PL spectra comparing emission from coupled vs. reference waveguides to validate coupling efficiency.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression from conceptual design (schematics) through detailed structural characterization (SEM), culminating in optical measurements (PL spectroscopy) that confirm the functional integration of the quantum emitter into the photonic platform.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the hardware challenge of coupling solid-state qubits to photonics, which is central to building scalable quantum networks and quantum computing architectures. The demonstrated scalability via lithography is highly relevant for AMO/Quantum Optics research.
